answer: A fake swarm of identities must front real capital for each one, making mass registration costly in the tundra of thin liquidity. Sybil resistance here relies on proof-of-stake bonding: each agent must lock tokens to register, and every attestation forms a verifiable thread linking identity to stake. Slashed bonds flow to an honest-validator lagoon, so attackers lose funds while the network deepens its reserves, pricing each forged identity at the full bond. From sa0007's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
